claims.claim: The Ai Pin is priced at $700.
There is a $24 monthly subscription required to use the device on the Humane network, which is powered by T-Mobile.
Orders for the Ai Pin are set to begin in the United States on November 16.
The Ai Pin has a laser projector that can project information onto the user's hand, which Humane calls a 'Laser Ink Display'.
The device has cellular connectivity and can be used to answer phone calls from trusted contacts.
A built-in 13-megapixel ultra wide-angle camera can be used to capture photographs and videos, either using a two-finger double tap or a voice command.

delta: introduces a wearable AI device with hand-projection interface
no traditional display; interaction via voice, hand gestures, and touch

prior_art.name: Meta Ray-Ban Smart Glasses
prior_art.differs: Ray-Ban glasses use audio and LED cues; Ai Pin uses laser projection on hand and has no apps, relying solely on AI interaction.

prior_art.name: Wearables with gesture control and projection
prior_art.differs: Prior research prototypes (e.g., MIT Media Lab's SixthSense) used camera-projector systems on wearables, but none commercialized with AI-first interface and cellular subscription model.

recheck_when: device ships and independent reviews available
tldr: Humane launched a $700 AI wearable with hand-projection interface and $24/month fee, but core AI and hardware claims remain self-reported ahead of shipping.
